key_insight: The paper introduces a hardware-efficient variational ansatz whose Fubini–Study metric is exactly diagonal, enabling metric-aware quantum optimization and time evolution without auxiliary metric circuits or matrix inversion.
engineering_relevance: This reduces circuit depth and classical overhead for variational quantum algorithms, while preserving controllability for state preparation, sampling, and dynamics on near-term hardware.
method: Binary-tree parametrization of n-qubit states with a closed-form diagonal pullback metric
Quantum natural gradient, variational real/imaginary-time evolution, and Haar sampling performed directly on tree parameters
Gauge-pruning and reparameterization variants reduce two-qubit gate counts and can enforce exact spin adaptation
evidence_signal: The abstract reports reference-level accuracy on small-molecule electronic-structure problems and half-filled Hubbard quenches using one to three orders of magnitude fewer two-qubit gates than leading alternatives.
watch_item: The bare ansatz is classically simulable in the sector size k, so quantum advantage depends on composing it with a classically hard dressing and on careful circuit compilation.
paper_title: A hardware-efficient variational ansatz with an exact diagonal metric for real- and imaginary-time evolution and Haar sampling
